paragraphs.en: In 1916, two girls of {wealthy} families, best friends from Auburn, N.Y.—Dorothy Woodruff and Rosamond Underwood—traveled to a {settlement} in the {Rocky} {Mountains} to teach in a {remote} one-room {schoolhouse} with only a {blackboard} and some basic supplies.While most of their peers ( (同龄人) ) chose to {marry} or engage in dull social activities, the two women embarked on a journey that would take them far from the {parties} , fine {silk} clothing and the {buffets} they were used to, leaving behind the {estate} of their rich families.So for them to move to Elkhead, Colorado, to {instruct} the children, {whose} {shoes} were held together with {string} , was a surprise.The mountains of Colorado, {dotted} with {mines} and wandering {goats} , were a stark ( (鲜明的) ) contrast to their daily life.Their stay in Elkhead is the subject of Nothing Daunted : The Unexpected Education of Two Society Girls in the West, by Dorothy Wickenden-a magazine editor and Dorothy Woodruff's {granddaughter} .
paragraphs.cn: 1916年，来自纽约州奥本市的两位 <u> 富 </u> 家千金——多萝西·伍德拉夫和罗莎蒙德·安德伍德，这对挚友一同前往 <u> 落基山脉 </u> 的一个 <u> 定居点 </u> ，在一所 <u> 偏远的 </u> 单间 <u> 校舍 </u> 里教书，那里只有一块 <u> 黑板 </u> 和一些基本的教具。当时，她们的大多数同龄人都选择 <u> 结婚 </u> ，或参加无聊的社交活动，而这两位女性却开启了一段旅程，远离了她们习以为常的 <u> 聚会 </u> 、精致的 <u> 丝绸 </u> 服饰和 <u> 自助餐 </u> ，离开了自家的豪 <u> 宅 </u> 。她们搬到科罗拉多州的埃尔克黑德，去 <u> 教 </u> 那些 <u> 鞋子 </u> 要用 <u> 绳子 </u> 绑到一起的孩子们，这一举动令人惊讶。科罗拉多州的山脉上 <u> 布满 </u> 了 <u> 矿场 </u> ，还有四处游荡的 <u> 山羊 </u> ，与她们的日常生活形成了鲜明的对比。她们在埃尔克黑德的这段经历，正是多萝西·威肯登——一位杂志编辑，也是多萝西·伍德拉夫的 <u> 孙女 </u> ——所著的《无所 <u> 畏惧 </u> ：两位上流社会女孩在西部的 <u> 意外 </u> 历练》一书的主题。

paragraphs.en: Why did they go then? Well, they wanted to do something useful.Soon, however, they realized what they had {undertaken} .
paragraphs.cn: 那么，她们为什么要去西部呢？好吧，是因为她们想做点有用的事。不过，她们很快就意识到了自己 <u> 肩负 </u> 的任务。

paragraphs.en: They moved in with a local family, the Harrisons, and, like them, had little {privacy} , rare {baths} , and a blanket of snow on their {quilt} when they {woke} up in the morning—harsh conditions that would make most society men or women {quit} .Some mornings, Rosamond and Dorothy would arrive at the schoolhouse to find the children {weeping} from the cold.In spring, the snow was replaced by {mud} over ice.One can imagine them learning to {sew} their own clothes, and perhaps {mending} their students’ {torn shirts} and {shorts} .They wrote letters home, sharing their experiences with their families and {brothers} back east.They never showed {pity} , instead embracing their new life with {determination} .
paragraphs.cn: 她们住进了当地的哈里森家，和这家人一样，几乎没有 <u> 隐私 </u> ，很少 <u> 洗澡 </u> ，早上 <u> 醒来 </u> 时 <u> 被子 </u> 上盖着一层薄雪。这样恶劣的条件会让大多数上流社会男女 <u> 放弃 </u> 。有些早晨，罗莎蒙德和多萝西赶到校舍，只见孩子们冻得直 <u> 哭 </u> 。春天，积雪会被冰上的 <u> 泥泞 </u> 取代。可以想象，她们学着 <u> 缝制 </u> 自己的衣服，也许还会 <u> 修补 </u> 学生 <u> 破洞的衬衫 </u> 和 <u> 短裤 </u> 。她们写信回家，与留在东部的家人和 <u> 兄弟 </u> 分享她们的经历。她们毫无自 <u> 怜 </u> 之意，而是 <u> 坚定 </u> 地拥抱新的生活。

paragraphs.en: In Wickenden's book, she expanded on the history of the West and also on {feminism} , as it was uncommon for young {educated} women to step beyond the traditional roles of {wives} and mothers.Her book lets readers {witness} the frontier life of the early 20th century.A {hair-raising} {section} concerns the building of the {railroads} , which entailed ( (牵涉) ) {drilling} through the Rockies, often in {blinding} {snowstorms} .The book ends with Rosamond and Dorothy's return to Auburn.
paragraphs.cn: 威肯登在书中补充了美国西部的历史和 <u> 女权主义 </u> 相关的内容，因为在当时， <u> 受过教育的 </u> 年轻女性鲜少能够突破 <u> 妻子 </u> 、母亲等传统角色。她的书让读者 <u> 见证 </u> 了20世纪初的边疆生活。书中有一 <u> 段惊心动魄的 </u> 描写讲述了修建 <u> 铁路 </u> 的过程：工人们常常要冒着 <u> 让人视线模糊 </u> <u> 的暴风雪 </u> 在落基山脉 <u> 开凿 </u> 隧道。这本书以罗莎蒙德和多萝西回到奥本市结束。

paragraphs.en: Wickenden is a very good {storyteller} .The {sweep} of the {land} and the stoicism ( (坚忍) ) of the people move her to some beautiful writing.Here is a picture of Dorothy Woodruff, on her {horse} , looking down from a hill top:“When the sun slipped behind the mountains, it {shed} a rosy {glow} all around them.Then a full {moon} rose.The snow was marked only by small animals: foxes, coyotes, {mice} , and {varying} hares, which turned white in the winter.”
paragraphs.cn: 威肯登是一位很好的 <u> 讲述者 </u> 。这片 <u> 广阔 </u> 的 <u> 土地 </u> 和人们的坚忍不拔驱使她创作出了优美的篇章。她描写了这样一幅画面：多萝西·伍德拉夫骑在 <u> 马 </u> 上，从山顶俯瞰——“当太阳滑落到山后，在周围 <u> 洒下 </u> 了玫瑰色的 <u> 光 </u> ；然后，一轮满 <u> 月 </u> 升起。雪地上只有小动物留下的足迹——狐狸、郊狼、 <u> 老鼠 </u> ，还有随冬季换上白毛的 <u> 变色 </u> 野兔。” 5NoOncib/NjiX02BpMIzP4m+378Hw1xTRxUdPaP/PFjKUFq4K2G7tp6ZLYoCE601yW1W39VMdLmovFdSHs4nVQ==
